messages:
lee: heads-up — I kicked off a payload-sampler run in ap-southeast to probe tokens/sec variance during the promo spike. Started ~10m ago.
ashley: what sampler args did you use (batch, max_tokens, warmup)?
lee: config: ```sampler --batch 8 --max-tokens 1024 --warmup=20 --mix=chat,long```
lee: early numbers: short-chat path ~220k tokens/sec per GPU, long-tail requests drop to ~60k tokens/sec and push CUDA util down.
vik: can you paste the perf snapshot / nvidia stats?
lee: quick paste: ```
GPU  TOKENS/S  UTIL%
0    220000     92
1     60000     45
```
ashley: that split is classic mixing penalty — long requests don't amortize kernel init and KV cache warms. Our current capacity model assumes single tokens/sec mean; need 95th-token-tail factor.
vik: agreed. Also noticed preemptible evictions spiked when the long-tail hit — scheduling churn increases tail latency. Any numbers on evictions?
lee: preemptible evictions up 3x in the last 15m during the run. Latency p95 jumped ~120ms for small requests when eviction+requeue happened.
ashley: proposal: add an explicit "long-horizon" headroom bucket in the throughput model (reserve ~20% capacity), route by token-estimate header to isolated nodes, fallback to preemptible with higher tail-latency SLA.
vik: we should simulate cost/latency tradeoffs: reserve extra capacity in-region vs spill to cheaper preemptible in other region. Example roughs: reserved-monthly apac GPU pool ~$18k, preemptible-spill cost ~$6k/month but adds ~15% p95 latency.
lee: also saw regional network egress to us-west at 85% during promo — if we spill cross-region that egress becomes a bottleneck. Need to fold egress headroom into routing policy.
ashley: +1. Action items: 1) run a detailed sim with realistic mix (short:60%, medium:30%, long:10%) and preemptible churn, 2) update headroom model to include 95th-token-tail, 3) produce cost sensitivity table for reserved vs preemptible (apac/us-west).
vik: I'll own #2 and add a token-tail multiplier into the capacity calculator. lee -> please run #1 and attach sim id. I'll collaborate on the sim config.
lee: queued sim via orion-bot: `orion-bot: queued simulation 4521, config=payload-sampler-longtail, vms=120, seed=2026-03-18` :hourglass_flowing_sand:
orion-bot: simulation 4521 started — ETA ~42m.
ashley: while sim runs, temp mitigation: bump default overhead in autoscaler from 10% to 25% for apac pools for next 24h. Any objections?
lee: +1 (helps until we validate sim).
vik: +1
ashley: ok opening runbook PR to make the bump and add a note to routing docs about token-estimate header.
lee: adding notes + linking sim id to weekly capacity doc.
vik: one more: track KV cache hit ratio in the sim. Current prod hit ~12% which is low — caching improvements could buy us ~15% effective throughput on short chats.
ashley: agreed — add cache-hit to sim metrics.
lee: ack. I'll post sim results to this thread and update the capacity spreadsheet when done.
ashley: thanks all.
thread_text_preview: lee kicked off a payload-sampler in ap-southeast to probe tokens/sec variance; short path ~220k tps/GPU, long-tail ~60k; preemptible evictions spiked. Action: run sim, bump overhead to 25%, add long-tail headroom and cache-hit metrics.
